title: How Burglars Break In Using a Plastic Card — and How a Locksmith Stops It
description:
On a lot of front doors in this country, a plain plastic card is all it takes. Not because the card is clever. Because of the little angled latch that holds the door shut.

I am not going to show you how it is done. The internet has plenty of that. This video is about WHY it works, and how to stop it, cheapest fix first.

In this video:
- Why a locked knob does nothing to the spring latch (and why "latched" is not "locked")
- The small deadlatch plunger most keyed knobs already have, and why it stops working when a door sags
- A ten second test you can do tonight with a sheet of paper
- Six fixes in order of cost: using the deadbolt you have, a $3 hinge screw, lining up the strike, a knob with a deadlatch, a latch guard, and a real one-inch deadbolt

Prices are rough ranges and depend on the store, the brand and your door. Some latch guards will not fit some doors, and if you rent, ask before you drill.
